cases.issue_title: [bug]: fully cancelling a paid seated booking refunds only one seat's payment
cases.issue_body:
### Issue Summary

On a seated paid event, every attendee booking the same time slot creates a separate `Payment` record, but all of those payments belong to the same booking. When the host fully cancels that booking and the event's **Refund on cancellation** policy is set to **Always** or **Days**, only one attendee is refunded. The remaining attendees have their bookings cancelled but their successful payments are never refunded, and no error is reported.

The refund flow currently resolves only the first successful payment for a booking. Although the cancellation flow passes all booking payments into the refund handler, `processPaymentRefund.ts` selects a single payment via `payment.find((p) => p.success)` and issues only one refund request, silently ignoring the rest.

This is different from **#29664**, which affected the booking confirmation page UI. This issue causes real payment refunds to be skipped.

---

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a paid event type with:

   * `seatsPerTimeSlot > 1`
   * a payment provider (e.g. Stripe) connected
   * **Refund on cancellation** set to **Always** (or **Days**).
2. Have two (or more) different attendees book and successfully pay for the same time slot.
3. As the host, cancel the entire booking (not removing an individual seat/attendee).
4. Check the payment provider (e.g. Stripe) dashboard for refunds.

---

### Actual Results

* Only the first successful payment associated with the booking is refunded.
* The remaining successful payments are left untouched.
* The booking is cancelled for every attendee, but the other attendees remain charged.
* No error or warning is surfaced.

---

### Expected Results

* Every successful payment associated with the cancelled booking should be refunded, subject to the configured refund policy (Always/Days and any applicable cutoff).
* If multiple attendees paid for the same booking, each successful payment should receive its own refund.

---

### Technical details

* **Type:** Backend payment/refund logic bug.
* **Reproduces on:** Current `main`.
* **Browser / Node.js:** Not browser-dependent (backend issue).
* **Affected code:**

  * `packages/features/bookings/lib/payment/processPaymentRefund.ts`

    * Uses `payment.find((p) => p.success)`, refunding only the first successful payment.
  * `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`

    * Correctly passes all booking payments (`payment: true`) into the refund flow, but only one is ultimately processed.
* **Impact:** Occurs only when:

  * the event has multiple seats,
  * multiple attendees have paid,
  * and the event uses automatic refunds on cancellation.

---

### Evidence

The issue was reproduced with automated tests.

* **Unit test (`processPaymentRefund.test.ts`)**

  * Created a booking containing two successful payments.
  * Expected `handlePaymentRefund` to be called once per successful payment.
  * On current `main`, only one refund is issued, confirming the bug.
  * After changing the implementation to refund every successful payment, the test passes.

* **Integration test (`handleCancelBooking.test.ts`)**

  * Cancelled a seated booking with multiple successful payments.
  * Verified that `handleCancelBooking` correctly passes all payments into `processPaymentRefund`.
  * Confirms the loss occurs inside `processPaymentRefund`, where only the first successful payment is selected for refund.

cases.issue_title: Test push notification opens https://app.cal.com instead of the self-hosted Cal.diy instance
cases.issue_body:
### Issue Summary

When a user enables push notifications, the server immediately sends a "Test Notification". The notification payload hardcodes `url: "https://app.cal.com/"`. The service worker uses exactly that `data.url` to navigate when the notification is clicked (`self.clients.openWindow(url)`), so on any self-hosted Cal.diy instance the test notification sends the user to **cal.com**, not their own deployment. Cal.diy is self-host-only, so this is wrong for the entire intended audience.

Every other place in the codebase that needs the app URL uses `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBAPP_URL || "https://app.cal.com"` (see `CalendarEventBuilder.ts`, `getPublicEvent.ts`, `RegularBookingService.ts`, etc.)  this handler is the only one that hardcodes the URL with no env fallback.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Self-host Cal.diy with `NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBAPP_URL` set to your own domain.
2. Sign in, go to settings, and enable push notifications.
3. Receive the "Test Notification" and click it.

### Actual Results

- The notification opens `https://app.cal.com/` (the public Cal.com app), not the user's own instance.

### Expected Results

- The notification should open the configured instance URL, e.g. `WEBAPP_URL` from `@calcom/lib/constants` (or `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_WEBAPP_URL`).

### Technical details

- The hardcoded URL: https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/main/packages/trpc/server/routers/loggedInViewer/addNotificationsSubscription.handler.ts#L68
- The service worker consumes `data.url` here: https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/main/apps/web/public/service-worker.js#L86-L94
- While in this file, two adjacent robustness/i18n nits are worth fixing in the same PR:
  - `JSON.parse(subscription)` at https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/main/packages/trpc/server/routers/loggedInViewer/addNotificationsSubscription.handler.ts#L32 is not wrapped in try/catch — malformed JSON throws an uncaught error and returns a 500 instead of a clean `BAD_REQUEST`.
  - The notification `title`/`body` (lines 66–67) are hardcoded English and aren't localized to the user's locale.

### Evidence

https://github.com/calcom/cal.diy/blob/main/packages/trpc/server/routers/loggedInViewer/addNotificationsSubscription.handler.ts#L60-L74

cases.issue_title: Calendar subscription sync ignores Cal.diy iCalUIDs
cases.issue_body:
### Issue Summary

Calendar subscription sync currently filters incoming calendar events by checking whether the event `iCalUID` ends with `@cal.com`.

However, Cal.diy generates booking iCalUIDs using the configured app name. In a default Cal.diy setup, `APP_NAME` defaults to `Cal.diy`, so generated booking UIDs can look like:

`test-booking-uid@Cal.diy`

Because the sync filter only accepts `@cal.com`, valid Cal.diy booking events can be skipped during calendar subscription sync. This means changes made from a connected calendar, such as cancelling or moving a synced booking event, may not be processed for default/self-hosted Cal.diy bookings.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a default Cal.diy setup where `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME` is not overridden.
2. Create a booking that gets an iCalUID using the default app name, for example `test-booking-uid@Cal.diy`.
3. Pass a calendar subscription event with that iCalUID into `CalendarSyncService.handleEvents`.
4. Observe that the event is filtered out before cancellation or reschedule handling runs.

### Actual Results

- Calendar subscription sync only processes events whose `iCalUID` ends with `@cal.com`.
- Valid Cal.diy iCalUIDs such as `test-booking-uid@Cal.diy` are ignored.
- The booking repository is never queried for the booking UID.
- Calendar-side changes may not sync back into Cal.diy.

### Expected Results

- Calendar subscription sync should process Cal-managed booking events generated by Cal.diy.
- UIDs ending in the default Cal.diy suffix should be accepted.
- Legacy `@cal.com` UIDs should continue to work.
- External calendar UIDs such as `@google.com` or `@external.com` should still be ignored.

### Technical details

- `APP_NAME` defaults to `Cal.diy` in `packages/lib/constants.ts`.
- iCalUID generation uses `APP_NAME` in `packages/emails/lib/getICalUID.ts`.
- Calendar subscription sync currently filters only `@cal.com` in `packages/features/calendar-subscription/lib/sync/CalendarSyncService.ts`.

### Evidence

I reproduced this with a focused unit test around `CalendarSyncService.handleEvents`.

A regression test using:

`test-booking-uid@Cal.diy`

fails with the current `@cal.com`-only filter because the event is not processed.

After updating the filter to accept Cal-managed iCalUID suffixes, the targeted calendar sync test passes:

`yarn vitest run packages/features/calendar-subscription/lib/sync/__tests__/CalendarSyncService.test.ts`

Result:

`21 tests passed`

cases.issue_title: Add-on (priced booking field) charges are dropped for additional seat bookers on paid seated events
cases.issue_body:
### Issue Summary

On a paid event that has both `seatsPerTimeSlot` set **and** priced booking fields (e.g. a `number` "tickets" field, or a priced `select`/`checkbox`/`boolean`/`radio` option), only the **first** booker for a slot is charged for their add-ons. Every **subsequent** seat booker is charged the **base price only** — their add-on selections are silently dropped from the payment, so the organizer loses that revenue on every seat after the first.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a paid event type (e.g. Stripe, base price $10) with `seatsPerTimeSlot: 3`.
2. Add a priced booking field — e.g. a `number` field named "tickets" at $5 each.
3. **Booker A** (first seat) books and selects `tickets = 3` → charged $10 + 3×$5 = **$25** (correct).
4. **Booker B** (second seat, joining the same slot) selects `tickets = 3`.

Why it's a bug: the first booker for a slot falls back to the regular booking path, which charges add-ons; subsequent seat bookings go through a different path that does not.

### Actual Results

* Booker B is charged **$10** (base price only); their `tickets = 3` add-on ($15) is never added to the payment.
* The organizer loses the add-on revenue for every seat after the first.

### Expected Results

* Every seat booker is charged the base price plus their selected add-ons, exactly like the first booker (Booker B should be charged **$25**).

### Technical Details

* The first seat falls back to `RegularBookingService`, which passes `bookingFields` to `handlePayment` (`packages/features/bookings/lib/service/RegularBookingService.ts:2308`).
* Subsequent seats route through `createNewSeat`, whose `handlePayment(...)` call **omits `bookingFields`** (and `locale`) (`packages/features/bookings/lib/handleSeats/create/createNewSeat.ts:262`).
* In `handlePayment`, the add-on pricing loop is gated by `if ((bookingFields || []).length > 0)` (`packages/features/bookings/lib/handlePayment.ts:81`), so when `bookingFields` is undefined, the add-ons are never computed and `totalAmount` remains at the base price.
* Not browser-specific; this is backend booking/payment logic.

### Evidence

* Verified by tracing the two `handlePayment` call sites. Only `RegularBookingService` passes `bookingFields`; `createNewSeat` does not. Also confirmed the add-on gate in `handlePayment`.
* Covered by a new unit test asserting that `createNewSeat` forwards `bookingFields` to `handlePayment`. The test **fails** on current `main` (called without `bookingFields`) and **passes** with the fix.
* A PR containing the fix and test is ready.

cases.issue_title: Filtering on Boolean columns has a limitation in Snowflake (and possibly other databases)
cases.issue_body:
### Bug description

In chart creator, I can't apply a filter on a Boolean column (e.g. to just return rows where the column is `True`) when using Snowflake.

The generated Snowflake SQL isn't valid, because `IS True` isn't valid in Snowflake. This is the generated SQL:

```
SELECT COUNT(*) AS "count" 
FROM flights.fct_flight_stats 
WHERE "IS_CANCELLED" IS true
 LIMIT 5000
```

`IS` can only be used to evaluate NULL-ness in Snowflake, not for filtering values (read more [here](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/constructs/where#usage-notes) and [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/76759093/how-to-query-with-filter-boolean-column-with-is-in-snowflake)). I suspect this is also true for some other databases, but I haven't researched thoroughly. 

The alternative would be to have menu options for `= True` and `= False`, for Boolean columns.

**Version**

Preset Cloud // Apache Superset 4.2.0.5

**Workarounds**

1. The `IN` option can be used in combination with and limiting the values to `True`.  
- However, if the generated SQL errored previously, the IN option mysteriously disappears in the UI for this Boolean column. I suspect this is because Superset isn't aware of valid values to fetch that would work for `IN`. I'm happy to open a separate issue for this if the community would like!

2. Use the Custom SQL tab and manually specify `= True`.

cases.issue_title: HOURS OFFSET applies only to 1 time column, it should apply to all temporal columns in the dataset
cases.issue_body:
In Dataset Settings there is an option called "HOURS OFFSET". 
When you have only one time column, it's working as expected: it adds the corresponding number of hours to the time column while outputting it on the chart. However, when you have more than one temporal columns, the number of hours is logically expected to be added to all of them. Now it adds to only the one column that is selected as the "TIME COLUMN" in the chart.

#### How to reproduce the bug

1. Create a dataset with more than one temporal field (e.g. Creation and expiration dates, as in the screencast),
2. Add "HOURS OFFSET" to the dataset settings (e.g. 4) and save the dataset,
3. Choose a "TIME COLUMN" in the Time settings of the chart and click Update,
4. Choose another "TIME COLUMN" and click Update

### Expected results
X hours (set in "HOURS OFFSET") should be added to all temporal fields, regardless of the "TIME COLUMN" selected.

### Actual results
X hours are added to only one column, the one that is selected as the "TIME COLUMN" in the chart.

Note, that in the screencast, the "Expire Date" of the bottom row is actually equal to the "Agreement Creation Date" of the top row, but they are displayed with a 4-hour difference either way, because of the "HOURS OFFSET" option set.

#### Screenshots
https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43491361/220833739-32950223-19ba-40e4-be12-d09804c40fde.mp4

   
Note, that the "Expire Date" of the bottom row is actually equal to the "Agreement Creation Date" of the top row, but they are displayed with a 4-hour difference either way, because of the "HOURS OFFSET" option set.

cases.issue_title: DAP: 'invalid type: map, expected unit' on configurationDone response when adapter returns body={}
cases.issue_body:
### Summary

`vscode-js-debug` (the DAP adapter Helix's `js-debug-dap` block is wired for) returns `body: {}` on the `configurationDone` response. Helix declares `ConfigurationDone::Result = ()` (unit type), so `serde_json::from_value::<()>(Value::Object({}))` fails with:

```
Debugger configuration failed: failed to parse: invalid type: map, expected unit
```

The error is shown to the user via `Editor::set_error` in the `Initialized` event handler, but the debug session continues (`set_active_client` runs regardless). The adapter has already accepted the request and returned `success: true`, so the debugger is actually running — the error is misleading, not fatal.

### Reproduction Steps

**`~/.config/helix/languages.toml`**

```toml
[[language]]
name = "javascript"

[language.debugger]
name = "js-debug-dap"
transport = "tcp"
port-arg = "{} 127.0.0.1"
command = "node"
args = ["/path/to/js-debug/src/dapDebugServer.js"]
quirks = { absolute-paths = true }

[[language.debugger.templates]]
name = "source"
request = "launch"
completion = [{ name = "main", completion = "filename", default = "index.js" }]
args = { type = "pwa-node", program = "{0}", skipFiles = ["<node_internals>/**"] }
```

**Adapter install** (Microsoft's prebuilt `js-debug-dap` release tarball, not the VS Code extension):

```bash
mkdir -p ~/lib/js-debug && cd ~/lib/js-debug
curl -L -o js-debug-dap.tar.gz \
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-js-debug/releases/download/v1.117.0/js-debug-dap-v1.117.0.tar.gz
tar -xzf js-debug-dap.tar.gz && rm js-debug-dap.tar.gz
# Entry point: ~/lib/js-debug/js-debug/src/dapDebugServer.js
```

**Steps:**

1. `echo 'console.log("hello")' > /tmp/index.js`
2. `hx /tmp/index.js`
3. Set a breakpoint (`<space>gb` on line 1)
4. `:debug-start source<ret>index.js<ret>`

**Expected:** debug session starts, status bar shows "Debugged application started".

**Actual:** status bar shows `Debugger configuration failed: failed to parse: invalid type: map, expected unit`. The debuggee actually starts, but the error message implies failure.

## Captured raw DAP response

Verified against the adapter directly (no Helix in the loop):

```json
{"seq": 2, "type": "response", "request_seq": 3, "command": "configurationDone", "success": true, "body": {}}
```

vscode-js-debug returns `body: {}` on every `configurationDone` response. This is technically non-DAP-compliant — the spec for `configurationDone`'s response has no body — but the same `{}` body shape is used by many other adapters (JDTLS, etc.) and Helix handles it elsewhere via `serde_json::Value` result types.


### Helix log

<details><summary>~/.cache/helix/helix.log</summary>

```
helix_dap::transport [INFO] -> DAP {"type":"request","seq":3,"command":"configurationDone","arguments":{}}
helix_dap::transport [INFO] <- DAP {"seq":4,"type":"response","request_seq":3,"command":"configurationDone","success":true,"body":{}}
helix_dap::transport [INFO] <- DAP success in response to 3
helix_view::editor [ERROR] editor error: Debugger configuration failed: failed to parse: invalid type: map, expected unit
```

</details>

cases.issue_title: Diagnostics from roslyn-language-server don't appear until an edit
cases.issue_body:
### Summary

Diagnostics don't appear until an edit has been made in the buffer when using roslyn-language-server.

That's because helix fetches diagnostics only when the `Notification::Initialized` has been sent by the roslyn-language-server and not when `Notification::ProgressMessage` signals that work has finished.

When `Notification::Initialized` is received, no diagnostics are returned. But after progress message signals work has finished, the language server returns diagnostics (if we request them).

cases.issue_title: Highlighting of inline math equations in markdown
cases.issue_body:
### Summary

Certain flavors of markdown support inline equations written in latex syntax, e.g. `some text $E=mc^2$ more text`. While the markdown tree-sitter used by helix supports the injection of latex, it appears the dollar-sign delimiters are not passed along to the latex tree-sitter. In the example, this means the latex tree-sitter has no way to know that `E=mc^2` is an equation and should be highlighted accordingly. Instead, it is highlighted as ordinary text, which is easy to verify with a minimal `.tex` file.

Fixing the issue is as easy as replacing the last occurrence (and only the last occurrence) of `injection.include-unnamed-children` with `injection.include-children` in the file `runtime/queries/markdown.inline/injections.scm` since this will cause the dollar-sign delimiters to be passed to the latex tree-sitter. At least, this fixed the problem for me.

**NB** Since `include-unnamed-children` is a helix extension of tree-sitter, this is a bug with helix and not a bug with tree-sitter.

### Reproduction Steps

Run the commands below then open `test.md` and `test.tex` in helix to compare syntax highlighting. Make sure to apply a theme that uses a special color for `@markup.raw` since that is the scope applied to latex equations.

```bash
echo 'some text $E=mc^2$ more text' > test.md
cat > test.tex << 'EOF'
\documentclass{article}
\begin{document}

E=mc^2 (this is how equations appear in markdown files)

$E=mc^2$ (this is how equations should appear in markdown files)

\end{document}
EOF
```

N/A
